# Dainik Samachar — neatHack 2026 submission **An AI agent that reads the news for you.** Dainik Samachar plans the searches, scrapes and cleans the sources, ranks headlines by impact and writes cited briefings and stock research for Indian investors. Every story keeps its sources attached. | | | |---|---| | Demo video | [youtu.be/aiGtUomSRCU](https://youtu.be/aiGtUomSRCU) | | Code | [github.com/learner-enthusiast/dainikSamachar](https://github.com/learner-enthusiast/dainikSamachar) | | Commits on Entire | [entire.io/gh/learner-enthusiast/dainikSamachar](https://entire.io/gh/learner-enthusiast/dainikSamachar/commit/99293e01b128bb70db3439d496d22f72e297abad) (one example; every checkpointed commit has its own page) | | cfo.ai model | [Shared report](https://cfo.ai/s/Ida4SXIoVpU40HP7) · [workspace page](https://app.cfo.ai/digitale-india-7c43edf1/pages/f4dc1616-0348-4de6-8cc8-86f5728b7684) (needs a cfo.ai login) | | Live app | > TODO (Arnab): production URL | | API docs | `/docs/api` on the live app ([route source](app/docs/api)) | | Judges page | `/judges` on the live app ([source](app/judges/page.tsx)) | ```mermaid flowchart LR U["User (Clerk) or Pro API key"] --> W["Next.js 16 app + /api/v1"] W --> I["Inngest pipelines"] I --> A1["News agents"] I --> A2["Stock research agents"] I --> A3["Chat agents"] I --> A4["Newsletter editions"] A1 & A2 & A3 & A4 --> T[("SerpApi · Firecrawl · Upstox · OpenAI")] I --> DB[("Postgres + pgvector")] I -. "one trace per run" .-> N["Neatlogs"] T -. "credits per call" .-> PU[("ProviderUsage")] DEV["Claude Code + Cursor sessions"] -. "checkpoint per commit" .-> E["Entire"] PU & N -. "cost inputs" .-> C["cfo.ai / Ari"] ``` **Contents:** [cfo.ai](#1-cfoai--how-it-shaped-the-business-plan) · [Entire](#2-entire--evidence-of-how-it-was-built) · [Neatlogs](#3-neatlogs--what-i-traced-debugged-and-improved) · [Form answers](#form-answers-copy-paste) --- ## 1. cfo.ai — how it shaped the business plan ### What I asked Ari, and why Every Dainik Samachar request fans out into paid calls: SerpApi searches, Firecrawl scrapes, Upstox market data and several LLM calls. If one request costs more than the user pays, growth only makes the loss bigger, so the cost of an agent run is the main business risk. I asked Ari to act as the CFO. The brief was to: 1. inspect the repo, 2. map each pipeline to the paid services it calls, 3. verify the provider prices, 4. build unit economics per pipeline, 5. model three scenarios with sensitivity, 6. propose pricing tiers and a break-even point, 7. list the risks. > TODO (Arnab): paste the exact prompt you gave Ari, or confirm this summary is accurate. ### What Ari built Ari produced a seven-page model: Assumptions, Evidence, Unit economics, Operating forecast, Sensitivity, Pricing and Risks. It ran for **36m 27s** and exported `Financial model (6 pages).xlsx`, which is 331 KB. Ari's step log shows it reconciling tier prices, checking the sensitivity cases, and checking risk notes and provider-source coverage ([screenshot 3](docs/hackathon/cfo-3.webp)). On the method, the model is explicit that it is a planning model, not accounting. Token counts are estimates grounded in the code's stages, not production traces. Costs are at nominal provider prices, not invoice-derived actuals. ### Key findings | Metric | Value | Label at source | Source | |---|---|---|---| | Cost per clean run, news briefing | **$0.20** | estimated | [Unit economics](docs/hackathon/cfo-1.webp) | | Cost per clean run, API research job | $0.14 | estimated | [Unit economics](docs/hackathon/cfo-1.webp) | | Cost per clean run, conversation session | $0.11 | estimated | [Unit economics](docs/hackathon/cfo-1.webp) | | Cost per clean run, stock report | $0.08 | estimated | [Unit economics](docs/hackathon/cfo-1.webp) | | Cost per clean run, news research | $0.04 | estimated | [Unit economics](docs/hackathon/cfo-1.webp) | | Searches per clean news briefing | 12 (stock report: 6) | estimated | [Unit economics](docs/hackathon/cfo-1.webp) | | LLM calls per clean run | briefing 20 · chat 25 · stock report 4 | estimated | [Unit economics](docs/hackathon/cfo-1.webp) | | Attempted runs per month | 8,030 (Oct-26) → 9,868.99 (May-27) | forecast | [Operating forecast](docs/hackathon/cfo-2.webp) | | Pro subscription | ₹199 / month | assumed (matches [`services/billing/pricing.ts`](services/billing/pricing.ts)) | [Assumptions](docs/hackathon/cfo-3.webp) | | API price | ₹20 / job | assumed | [Assumptions](docs/hackathon/cfo-3.webp) | | Paid conversion · MAU growth | 8% · 3% / month | assumed | [Assumptions](docs/hackathon/cfo-3.webp) | | Target margin | 0.7 | assumed | [Assumptions](docs/hackathon/cfo-3.webp) | **The headline finding is that a news briefing is the most expensive run: an estimated $0.20, which is 2.5× a stock research report ($0.08).** Search drives the cost. Of the briefing's $0.20, $0.12 is search, from 12 searches per clean run. ```mermaid xychart-beta title "Estimated cost per clean run (USD, cfo.ai)" x-axis ["News briefing", "API research job", "Conversation", "Stock report", "News research"] y-axis "USD" 0 --> 0.25 bar [0.20, 0.14, 0.11, 0.08, 0.04] ``` | Pipeline | Clean-run cost (USD) | of which search | Expected AI cost per attempt | |---|---|---|---| | News briefing | 0.20 | 0.12 | 0.07 | | API research job | 0.14 | 0.09 | 0.04 | | Conversation session | 0.11 | 0.08 | 0.02 | | Stock report | 0.08 | 0.06 | 0.01 | | News research | 0.04 | 0.03 | 0.01 | All of these are cfo.ai estimates.

### Decisions it drove No commit in the repo yet shows a change made because of the model. The model takes the existing ₹199 Pro price and the API's per-plan limits ([`lib/api/v1/limits.ts`](lib/api/v1/limits.ts): 60 requests a minute and 50 pipeline jobs a day, both overridable by env) as inputs. So the honest list is next steps: - **Optimise briefings first.** Search is 60% of the briefing's estimated cost ($0.12 of $0.20), so caching and fewer queries per tier come first. - **Check the model's LLM estimate against measured traces.** The model estimates $0.01 of AI cost per stock report attempt. The two stock research runs I traced locally spent about $0.0435 and about $0.021 on LLM calls (see [§3](#cost-visibility)). Feed the measured numbers back into the model. - **Use real credit data.** Per-user SerpApi and Firecrawl credits are now recorded (see [§3](#cost-visibility)). The next model revision can use actual credits per run instead of assumed ones. > TODO (Arnab): if any pricing, quota or free-tier change was made because of Ari's model, add the commit > here and move it out of "next steps". --- ## 2. Entire — evidence of how it was built ### 2.1 How did you use Entire? - **Setup:** Entire is enabled on this repo with the Claude Code and Cursor agent hooks, and checkpoints sync to `origin` ([`.entire/settings.json`](.entire/settings.json)). - **Checkpoints on (almost) every commit:** **38 of the repo's 40 commits** carry an `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer, which is 37 unique checkpoints (`ef159a1` and `1601d33` share one). If one request costs more than the user pays, growth only makes the loss bigger, so the cost of an agent run is the main business risk. I asked Ari to act as the CFO. The brief was to: 1. inspect the repo, 2. map each pipeline to the paid services it calls, 3. verify the provider prices, 4. build unit economics per pipeline, 5. model three scenarios with sensitivity, 6. propose pricing tiers and a break-even point, 7. list the risks. > TODO (Arnab): paste the exact prompt you gave Ari, or confirm this summary is accurate. ### What Ari built Ari produced a seven-page model: Assumptions, Evidence, Unit economics, Operating forecast, Sensitivity, Pricing and Risks. It ran for **36m 27s** and exported `Financial model (6 pages).xlsx`, which is 331 KB. Ari's step log shows it reconciling tier prices, checking the sensitivity cases, and checking risk notes and provider-source coverage ([screenshot 3](docs/hackathon/cfo-3.webp)). On the method, the model is explicit that it is a planning model, not accounting. Token counts are estimates grounded in the code's stages, not production traces. Costs are at nominal provider prices, not invoice-derived actuals. ### Key findings | Metric | Value | Label at source | Source | |---|---|---|---| | Cost per clean run, news briefing | **$0.20** | estimated | [Unit economics](docs/hackathon/cfo-1.webp) | | Cost per clean run, API research job | $0.14 | estimated | [Unit economics](docs/hackathon/cfo-1.webp) | | Cost per clean run, conversation session | $0.11 | estimated | [Unit economics](docs/hackathon/cfo-1.webp) | | Cost per clean run, stock report | $0.08 | estimated | [Unit economics](docs/hackathon/cfo-1.webp) | | Cost per clean run, news research | $0.04 | estimated | [Unit economics](docs/hackathon/cfo-1.webp) | | Searches per clean news briefing | 12 (stock report: 6) | estimated | [Unit economics](docs/hackathon/cfo-1.webp) | | LLM calls per clean run | briefing 20 · chat 25 · stock report 4 | estimated | [Unit economics](docs/hackathon/cfo-1.webp) | | Attempted runs per month | 8,030 (Oct-26) → 9,868.99 (May-27) | forecast | [Operating forecast](docs/hackathon/cfo-2.webp) | | Pro subscription | ₹199 / month | assumed (matches [`services/billing/pricing.ts`](services/billing/pricing.ts)) | [Assumptions](docs/hackathon/cfo-3.webp) | | API price | ₹20 / job | assumed | [Assumptions](docs/hackathon/cfo-3.webp) | | Paid conversion · MAU growth | 8% · 3% / month | assumed | [Assumptions](docs/hackathon/cfo-3.webp) | | Target margin | 0.7 | assumed | [Assumptions](docs/hackathon/cfo-3.webp) | **The headline finding is that a news briefing is the most expensive run: an estimated $0.20, which is 2.5× a stock research report ($0.08).** Search drives the cost. ### Decisions it drove No commit in the repo yet shows a change made because of the model. The model takes the existing ₹199 Pro price and the API's per-plan limits ([`lib/api/v1/limits.ts`](lib/api/v1/limits.ts): 60 requests a minute and 50 pipeline jobs a day, both overridable by env) as inputs. So the honest list is next steps: - **Optimise briefings first.** Search is 60% of the briefing's estimated cost ($0.12 of $0.20), so caching and fewer queries per tier come first. - **Check the model's LLM estimate against measured traces.** The model estimates $0.01 of AI cost per stock report attempt. The two stock research runs I traced locally spent about $0.0435 and about $0.021 on LLM calls (see [§3](#cost-visibility)). Feed the measured numbers back into the model. - **Use real credit data.** Per-user SerpApi and Firecrawl credits are now recorded (see [§3](#cost-visibility)). The next model revision can use actual credits per run instead of assumed ones. > TODO (Arnab): if any pricing, quota or free-tier change was made because of Ari's model, add the commit > here and move it out of "next steps". --- ## 2. content.content:
### What I'd do next

1. **Build the eval loop:** a fixed dataset of queries, scorers and saved baseline vs. after reports with
   trace ids, so improvements have numbers.
2. **Fix `getCompetitors`:** use the instrument key format the endpoint expects, then show the before → after
   using the `upstox_error` detection.
3. **Sum cost onto the run's root:** each step's tokens and cost go on its own step span, but the root shows
   $0. Then the cfo.ai model can use measured cost per run and credits instead of estimates.

---
### 6. Neatlogs: what did you trace, debug or improve?

```text
I traced every workflow (stock research, chat, news, rerun, newsletter, embeddings) as one Neatlogs trace per user action: Clerk end user, workflow name, agent/tool/LLM spans, tokens and cost, with secrets masked. The trace context rides Inngest events, so multi-step runs stay in one trace (43-80 spans in real runs). The first stock research trace exposed a real bug: upstox.getCompetitors fails with UDAPI100011 (Invalid Instrument key) on every stock run. The agent kept going, but its reports lacked competitor data. Neatlogs flagged that run as Execution Failed. Traces also showed the report synthesizer dominates cost ($0.042 of ~$0.0435 per run, 38k input tokens), and I set detection thresholds from those numbers (tokens > 45k, cost > $0.05, Upstox error regex). I also linked per-user SerpApi/Firecrawl credits to each trace by runId.
```
### 1. How did cfo.ai shape your business plan?

```text
Every request fans out into paid SerpApi, Firecrawl, Upstox and LLM calls, so run cost is my main business risk. I asked Ari (cfo.ai) to act as CFO: inspect the repo, map each pipeline to its paid services, verify prices, and build unit economics, scenarios, sensitivity, pricing and risks. Ari built a 7-page model in 36m 27s. Key finding: a news briefing is my most expensive run at an estimated $0.20 per clean run, 2.5x a stock report ($0.08), and $0.12 of that is search. So briefings and search caching are where I optimise first. The model prices the ₹199/month Pro plan and ₹20 API jobs at an assumed 8% paid conversion. My traced stock runs spent $0.021-$0.0435 on LLM calls against the model's $0.01 estimate, so I'm feeding measured costs back in. Report: https://cfo.ai/s/Ida4SXIoVpU40HP7
```

### 2. How did you use Entire?
